entrypoints.summary: The PHP request handler accepts POST parameter filename, reads it with file_get_contents, and later uses it in an exec command.

affected_components.role: Accepts filename, uses it as a pathname, and constructs the GNU sort command.
Privileged helper reads /flag and writes its contents to stdout.
Builds the helper, makes /flag root-only, and sets the helper setuid-root.

preconditions: The Apache/PHP service must be reachable; Compose maps host port 9001 to container port 8080.
A client must send a POST request containing filename.
Any escalation from sort argument influence to /readflag execution and observable output is not established by supplied evidence.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A client-controlled filename string; no working payload is evidenced.
trigger_steps.summary: Send a POST request whose filename value is processed as a pathname and appended to the sort command.

capabilities.concept: influence over GNU sort option-or-operand parsing

mitigations.concept: allowlisted path resolution with non-option argument separation

relation_candidates.rationale: The handler directly supplies POST filename to file_get_contents.

relation_candidates.dst: influence over GNU sort option-or-operand parsing
relation_candidates.rationale: The same unallowlisted filename is appended to the sort command without an evidenced end-of-options delimiter.
file_get_contents is invoked on the supplied filename.
The image includes a setuid-root helper that prints /flag, but no artifact proves a payload can invoke it or expose its output.
relation_candidates.src: influence over GNU sort option-or-operand parsing

relation_candidates.dst: allowlisted path resolution with non-option argument separation
relation_candidates.rationale: Resolving only approved identifiers and separating arguments prevents arbitrary request text from being used as a pathname or interpreted as sort options.

impact.affected_asset: Server-side filesystem path selection and GNU sort command semantics; /flag is root-readable only in the supplied image.
impact.attacker_capability: Submit a filename value that the application attempts to read and includes in its GNU sort invocation.
impact.security_effect: Server-side pathname access is attacker-directed, and the GNU sort invocation may parse attacker-controlled text as options or operands; privileged-helper-based flag disclosure remains unproven.

causal_trace.summary: An HTTP client supplies the POST filename value.

The handler treats that value as both a server-side pathname and text appended after the fixed sort command; no demonstrated allowlist constrains it to the displayed files or establishes it as a non-option operand.

The handler calls file_get_contents on the supplied pathname and executes sort followed by escapeshellcmd-transformed supplied text; escapeshellcmd does not itself provide an allowlist or an explicit end-of-options boundary.

The request can cause server-side access attempts to attacker-specified paths and can influence GNU sort argument interpretation. The runtime also contains a setuid-root helper that reads and prints the root-only /flag, but no supplied trace establishes a working bridge from the request handler to helper invocation or flag disclosure.

failure.operation: PHP exec of a GNU sort command constructed by concatenating transformed POST filename text

primary_invariant.statement: A client-selected file identifier must resolve only to an approved server-side input, and it must be passed to GNU sort as an unambiguous non-option operand rather than as concatenated command text.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The POST filename is directly supplied to file_get_contents and concatenated into exec("sort " . escapeshellcmd($filename)) without an evidenced identifier-to-path allowlist or end-of-options delimiter.

quality.review_notes: Primary PHP and runtime artifacts establish the request-to-pathname and request-to-exec construction. No supplied PoC, HTTP trace, GNU sort behavior trace, execution result, patch, or request/response observation proves a usable option-injection payload, helper execution, or flag-output disclosure. The repository is a dataset mirror rather than established organizer provenance.

remediation.invariant_restored: Map a small approved client file identifier set to server-side paths, and invoke sort with a fixed program and argument vector in which the resolved pathname follows an explicit end-of-options boundary.
